newsitem.title: USA: Perry says no decision on Bosnia force in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Perry says no decision on Bosnia force in 1997.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Saturday no decision had been made on deploying U.S. troops in Bosnia next year.

In a statement Perry called a report in the New York Times misleading. The report quoted administration officials, NATO leaders and European diplomats as saying "active planning" was under way for a force of 15,000 to 30,000 troops that would remain in Bosnia at least through 1997.
Perry said NATO military advisers were considering four options and no decision had been made by NATO or the United States.

The options were: complete withdrawal of the current NATO force, a "deterrence force" to prevent outbreak of fighting, a "sustaining force" to provide security in Bosnia and a continuation of the current mission.
"These options are still being analysed by NATO military authorities," Perry said. He added the analysis would not be available for some days and he had made no recommendation to President Clinton.
The Times quoted a senior European diplomat as saying that although the United States had not specifically said it would put American troops on the ground next year "there are nods and winks."

The issue of having American troops in Bosnia beyond the previously announced pullout date at the end of this year is politically sensitive. Republicans have accused the administration of deceiving the public about a longer commitment.
